title: Swift Mock Exam: Fundamentals
description: 45 minutes focused entirely on the foundations of the language (Variables, Optionals, Collections, Functions, ARC, Value vs Reference Types).

questions.question: When you pass a Struct as a parameter to a function in Swift, what happens by default?
options: It is passed by reference.
It is passed by value, with a constant copy (let) being made.
It can be freely modified inside the function.
The compiler requires the use of unsafe pointers.
questions.explanation: Structs are Value Types and, by default, function parameters are constants.

questions.question: What is the correct way to safely unwrap multiple Optionals at once?
options: if let a = optA, let b = optB { }
if let a = optA && let b = optB { }
guard let a = optA, b = optB else { }
if optA != nil, optB != nil { let a = optA!, let b = optB! }
questions.explanation: Swift lets you chain Optional Bindings with commas.

questions.question: What does the mutating keyword allow in a Struct?
options: It allows it to inherit from a Class.
It allows its methods to modify the Struct's own properties.
It turns the Struct into a Class at compile time.
It marks the Struct for the Garbage Collector.
questions.explanation: Since Structs are immutable by default, methods that modify their values must be marked as mutating.

questions.question: What is the classic retain cycle created in closures, and how do you prevent it?
options: Closures do not create retain cycles in Swift.
It occurs when an object holds a strong reference to a closure, which in turn captures "self" strongly. It is resolved with [weak self].
It occurs with chained Structs. It is resolved with [unowned self].
It occurs in the delegate. It is resolved using "lazy".
questions.explanation: Closures are Reference Types and capture external variables strongly by default.

questions.question: In what scenario will a defer block be executed?
options: Right before the current scope exits (before the return takes effect).
Only if an error occurs and a catch is triggered.
As soon as it is declared.
On a secondary (background) thread.
questions.explanation: The defer block guarantees execution at the exact moment the scope is exited, which is ideal for cleaning up resources.

title: Apple Dev Mock Exam: iOS & Architecture
description: Focused on the UIKit and SwiftUI ecosystem and state management (MVVM). 10 questions, 30 minutes.

questions.question: In SwiftUI, how do you propagate changes in a state object (Reference Type) to update all connected Views?
options: By marking the object as @StateObject and using didSet.
By adopting ObservableObject in the class and using @Published on the properties.
By issuing a NotificationCenter.default.post().
By calling view.setNeedsDisplay().
questions.explanation: Classes must be ObservableObject, and properties that trigger rendering must be @Published.

questions.question: Which lifecycle modifier replaces UIKit's old viewDidAppear in SwiftUI?
options: .onAppear
.onLoad
.onReady
.task
questions.explanation: .onAppear runs the closure when the View appears on screen.

questions.question: When dealing with concurrency (async/await), what does @MainActor guarantee?
options: That the task will run in the background.
That the function or type will always operate on the Main Thread (the UI's main thread).
That the function will never cause a Data Race.
That the API will not block.
questions.explanation: All user interface operations must happen on the Main Thread; @MainActor enforces this behavior.

questions.question: When injecting data deep into the View hierarchy (SwiftUI), what is the best approach?
options: Passing it as a parameter in each View's init, View by View.
Using Global Variables (Singletons).
Using .environmentObject() or @Environment()
Saving to UserDefaults and reading it in every view.
questions.explanation: Environment is designed precisely for deep dependency injection without "prop drilling".

questions.question: In UIKit, when adding a subview programmatically using Auto Layout, what must NEVER be forgotten?
options: Calling view.layoutIfNeeded() immediately.
Setting translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
Setting the background color to transparent.
Making the view inherit from a UIButton.
questions.explanation: If this is not done, the manually created constraints will conflict with the automatic constraints converted from the old frame (autoresizing mask).

title: iOSLab Challenge (Apple Academy - Brazil)
description: Mock exam focused on the entrance exams of Apple Academies in Brazil. Tests reasoning, basic Swift logic and the ecosystem (5 questions, 15 minutes).

questions.question: In Swift, what is the main difference between let and var?
options: let declares a free variable, var declares a strict constant.
let declares a constant whose value cannot be changed, var declares a mutable variable.
let can only be used for numbers (Integers/Doubles), var for Strings.
let allocates on the Heap, var allocates on the Stack.
questions.explanation: The `let` keyword creates immutable constants, while `var` creates variables whose values can be changed during execution.

questions.question: If you try to force unwrap an Optional using ! and the value is nil, what happens?
options: The value will be automatically converted to 0 or an empty string.
The compiler will emit a warning, but will skip the line.
The app will "crash" (a fatal runtime error).
The variable will be removed from memory.
questions.explanation: Force unwrapping (`!`) a nil value causes a crash (Fatal Error: unexpectedly found nil). That is why we should always use if let or guard let.

questions.question: Which of the following types in Swift is a Reference Type?
options: Struct
Enum
Tuple
Class
questions.explanation: Classes are Reference Types. Structs, Enums and Tuples are Value Types in Swift.

questions.question: What does the "Delegate" pattern (Delegation) most commonly allow in the Apple ecosystem?
options: Running very heavy network tasks in the background.
Letting one object hand off responsibilities and events to another object (e.g., button or cell taps).
Drawing user interfaces declaratively.
Replacing the use of Struct inheritance.
questions.explanation: Delegation is a Design Pattern that lets one object delegate the responsibility of performing an action to another, common in UIKit (such as UITableViewDelegate).

questions.question: In Swift programming logic, what does the .count property return when called on an Array [1, 2, 3] after an .append(4)?
options: nil
questions.explanation: The .append(4) method adds one element, increasing the array's total from 3 to 4 elements.

title: Senior iOS Dev Interview (Latin America)
description: Advanced mock exam aimed at Mid-level/Senior roles. Explores MVVM, Memory Management (ARC), Concurrency and lifecycle. (5 questions, 25 minutes).

questions.question: When working with closures that run asynchronous tasks and capture "self", why do we often use [weak self]?
options: To make sure the closure runs faster on the Main Thread.
To avoid memory leaks caused by retain cycles (Retain Cycles).
Because the Swift 5 compiler requires weak in all escaping closures.
To temporarily turn the class into a value type.
questions.explanation: If an object holds a strong reference to a closure, and the closure captures the object strongly, a Retain Cycle occurs and neither is ever deallocated from memory.

questions.question: What is the main responsibility of the ViewModel layer in the MVVM architecture?
options: Drawing the interface (UI) programmatically using SwiftUI or UIKit.
Strictly holding the serialized data of the local database.
Mediating between the Model and the View, abstracting presentation logic and managing visual state.
Exclusively handling flow routing (Routing) between screens.
questions.explanation: The ViewModel processes data from the Model and formats it into observable properties so the View can react (Data Binding), taking that complexity out of the Views (or ViewControllers).

questions.question: With the introduction of Swift Concurrency, what does the "await" keyword indicate?
options: It blocks the current thread indefinitely until the task finishes.
It marks a suspension point, where the thread can be freed for other work while waiting for the result.
It forces the immediate start of a task on a serial GCD queue.
It merely injects a completion handler asynchronously.
questions.explanation: `await` indicates a Suspension Point. The system can suspend that function's execution and use the current thread for something else until the asynchronous result arrives.

questions.question: When persisting structured data locally in an enterprise iOS app, which of the options below is NOT a primary (native) Apple mechanism?
options: Core Data
SwiftData
Realm
UserDefaults
questions.explanation: Realm is a powerful database widely used in the industry, but it is third-party (maintained by MongoDB). Core Data and SwiftData are Apple's native persistence frameworks.

questions.question: In the lifecycle of a UIViewController (UIKit), which method is called immediately after the subviews have had their sizes adjusted and Auto Layout has been applied?
options: viewDidLoad()
viewWillAppear()
viewDidAppear()
viewDidLayoutSubviews()
questions.explanation: `viewDidLayoutSubviews` is called after the layout system adjusts the bounds/frames of the child views. It is the ideal place to get real dimensions and draw gradients, for example.
